articles.title: Trump-Pezeshkian meeting on UNGA sidelines? US president 'open' to talks with Iran
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trump has expressed interest in meeting Iranian officials in New York during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assemb.
articles.body: US President Donald Trump has expressed interest in meeting Iranian officials in New York during the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, provided “the conditions are right”, CNN reported, citing a US official familiar with the matter.According to the official, discussions are under way over the possibility of a meeting on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. However, no formal encounter has been scheduled yet.The official said a potential meeting could instead involve some of Trump's top advisers travelling with him in New York. Internal discussions have focused on whether such a meeting could help the administration find a way to end the US war with Iran.There is also uncertainty within the US administration over whether the Iranian diplomats in New York have the backing of Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who has the final say on major matters, the official told CNN.It also remains unclear whether Iranian officials would agree to meet their US counterparts.Iran's scaled-down delegation at the UN General Assembly includes foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and President Masoud Pezeshkian.Both US secretary of state Marco Rubio and US ambassador to the UN Mike Waltz have said Trump remains “open” to talks with Iranian representatives.Waltz told CNN’s Kaitlan Collins on Wednesday that Trump “is always open” to discussions.“That’s a question I wish you could ask the Iranians is, will they sit down directly with us? And who is speaking for the ayatollah? That’s been a continuous issue,” Waltz said.Asked whether Trump planned to meet Pezeshkian in New York, Rubio said Washington was receptive to the possibility, although no meeting had been formally scheduled."We’re open to that. I don’t think anything is scheduled at this point, but we’re certainly open to something like that, especially if it has the prospects of leading to something positive," Rubio said in an interview with US broadcaster NBC.Rubio also reiterated Washington's position on Iran's nuclear programme, saying the central objective of any diplomatic engagement was to ensure that Tehran never obtains a nuclear weapon."And that is the fact that Iran can never have a nuclear weapon. They just simply can’t," Rubio said.Neither Washington nor Tehran has confirmed that a face-to-face meeting between Trump and Pezeshkian has been arranged.The possibility of a meeting comes as the nearly seven-month-old US-Iran conflict continues, with both sides issuing warnings amid the lack of a resolution.Trump said on Monday that Iran faced choices including "wiping Iran out," allowing its economy to "rot" or reaching a deal. He also said he remained in "deciding mode" over Washington's next steps."My question is, if and when do I blow the entire nation up," Trump said. "They better behave."Iran, meanwhile, has warned that any fresh US military action could widen the conflict.Hossein Mohebbi, spokesperson for Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, said Tehran would change both its weapons and the geographical scope of the conflict if Washington launched another attack."If a new aggression takes place, we will definitely change the weapons and geography of the war," Mohebbi said, according to Iran's semi-official Fars news agency.Trump on Tuesday addressed UN General Assembly, while his Iranian counterpart Pezeshkian is also expected in New York.The gathering could provide an opportunity for direct contact between Washington and Tehran, even as uncertainty remains over whether such a meeting will take place.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Shadrack Sibiya arrested: Top South African policeman charged with sexual offences
articles.summary: Shadrack Sibiya, who has made no comment, is alleged to have groomed a 16-year-old and raped an 18-year-old.
articles.body:
One of South Africa's highest ranking police officers has been charged with sexual offences at a brief appearance at a court north-west of Johannesburg.

The charges relate to allegations that Lt Gen Shadrack Sibiya sexually groomed a 16-year-old girl and raped an 18-year-old woman. He is also facing a charge of trafficking, which could mean that others may be arrested in relation to this case.

The suspended deputy police commissioner, who was detained on Monday, has made no comment.

The 59-year-old is due to appear in court again on 29 September for a bail application. Prosecutors are expected to oppose bail.

The state has also requested that the court change the prison where Sibiya will be held in the meantime as there are indications of a potential escape plan, national broadcaster SABC is reporting.

The case comes as the police service is in the spotlight at a major public inquiry over allegations of corruption and collusion with criminals.

The inquiry, known as the Madlanga Commission, began last September and has heard accusations that Sibiya received a gift of 20 impalas from an alleged criminal kingpin in exchange for a police contract.

articles.title: Erdogan slams Israel’s ‘genocidal mindset’ in blistering UN address
articles.summary: Turkish leader says UN has been forced into ‘dysfunction’ and was ‘bleeding out’ in Palestine, Lebanon, Sudan.
articles.body:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan has condemned Israeli actions in Gaza and the occupied West Bank in a blistering speech at the United Nations General Assembly.

In a speech that saw the Israeli delegation walk out and Palestinian representatives applaud, Erdogan addressed Israel’s continuing war crimes in Gaza and the escalation of settler pogroms in the occupied West Bank.

“With the support of [US President Donald] Trump, we contributed to a ceasefire. But despite this so-called ceasefire, more than 1,300 civilians have been murdered in Gaza,” he said.

Although Hamas and other Palestinian groups have accepted the second phase of the October ceasefire framework agreement, he said “Israel is not putting an end to its actions in Gaza and the West Bank is going through the most challenging time as the illegal Israeli settlers occupy the region”.

Erdogan described Gaza as “the most inhumane, most shameful concentration camp of our time”.

“We face a genocidal mindset that can never get enough of killing. No one with humanity, mercy or conscience can turn a blind eye,” he added.

Erdogan slammed the UN, saying it has failed to fulfil its obligations to establish peace and stability in conflict zones.

“Eighty-one years ago, the United Nations was formed to preserve global peace and stability, but unfortunately, the UN has failed to fulfil its duty,” he said.

Erdogan maintained that the UN has been forced into “dysfunction” and was “bleeding out” in Palestine, Lebanon and Sudan.

Erdogan also addressed the absence of Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas at the UN meeting of world leaders after the US denied the Palestinian leader a visa to enter the country – the second time in two years.

“Let it be known that although President Abbas is unable to be with us here in person, we will, as we did last year, continue to be the voice of a free and sovereign state of Palestine,” Erdogan said.

The Turkish president also addressed Russia’s war on Ukraine, saying the time had come to bring the conflict to an end.

“Our sincere hope is to end the Ukraine-Russia war by keeping Ukraine’s territorial integrity and sovereignty intact,” he said.
